questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am interested South Korean culture. I heard from others who stayed in Seoul that it was a great destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy. The host university was very helpful. Copenhagen University did not help me much.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You should live in Simple Spaces Korea. A great way to get to know other exchange students and the host is super friendly. It is affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My semester was fully online, so for me, it didn't matter to live off-campus. If you choose to live in Simple Spaces the subway is close and the drive is around 20 minutes from home to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to go to their website and then it is quite accessible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The KU GSC-Exchange/Visiting Student Team are very helpful. I asked them a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for 5 out of 6 classes that I wanted. The Add/Drop period is very good if you want to change your courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is ok.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't choose Korea for academic purposes, but I improved my English skills, so that was nice. Also, beware that you only need to sign up for 4 courses of 3 credits (12 credits in total). Then you might have time for a language Korean course, if you want to learn the language and your grade does not get transfered.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in most of my courses seemed very introduction-ish. I had to drop a course because the teacher's English was so bad.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It seemed more like high school. The exams does not count as much as in Copenhagen. You have midterms, tests, presentations, and also a part of your grade is participation. Nevertheless, I liked it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course Social Network Analysis was great!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite hard actually. Koreans tend to be a little bit narrow-minded. I experienced stuff as getting eggs thrown at me, yelled at in subways for talking, and denied access to restaurants and cafes. Their covid-19 rules were sometimes a bit discriminatory, and even though I was fully vaccinated I was never counted as so in their system. I know the pandemic is almost over, but it is something to consider. This was unpleasant, but I still had a great stay. The stay was just more Erasmus-oriented with a lot of Europeans compared to what I expected. Of course, I didn't attend school, so it might have been different if I had the opportunity to encounter other Korean students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: See the answer above.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their historical and cultural sights. I enjoyed "sight-seeing" very much and I had many great experiences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Live in Simple Spaces
2) If you study social science chose the course - Social Network Analysis. It was great. 
3) Be sure to exploit all the great historical and cultural options that Seoul offers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends all over in particular Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to know Koreans. They are not so open-minded and the covid-19-pandemic did not help in the situation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
